title: He Calls You by Name
speaker: Ryan Baird
summary: God's attention isn't split eight billion ways. It is fully on you. Like Mary at the tomb, hear him calling your name.
exhortation: As I read this a couple of days ago, it struck me that Jesus knows you. He sees you and cares for you with a fullness you can't really appreciate. If you've been a Christian for any length of time, you've heard that. But I don't know if we stop and appreciate how profound it is: the intensity and intimacy of God knowing us.

When we think of God giving his attention to every person in the world at once, if you're like me, you imagine it split eight billion ways. That would be amazing enough. But that isn't it at all. His attention is fully on you. He gives you his complete attention in a way you rarely get even from a close friend or a spouse.

You know the feeling when someone gives you their full attention, looking you in the eyes, listening and processing every word. It's almost uncomfortable. It feels almost sacred. We would do well to give people our full attention, because it's powerful. I think it feels holy because it's a glimpse of the way God treats us every single day. He isn't too busy or preoccupied. And his attention is far better than any person's, because he knows you, he listens to you, he cares for you and loves you. More than that, he wants to be with you. He moved heaven and earth to bring you near. That's what makes sin and turning away from God so insulting and painful: we take the Lord's attention and treat it with apathy.

So this morning, remember Mary at the tomb, so preoccupied with looking for Jesus that she didn't see him standing right in front of her. Our Lord knows us. He knows our frame. He knows you by name, and he is calling you just as he called Mary. He looks at you with an intensity and fullness that surpasses anything we experience on earth. Let's go to our Savior this morning and praise him with all we have.
prayer: Lord, thank you for calling us by name. You know us through and through, and seeing all of it, you still chose to save us, to die and give yourself as a ransom for us. Help us draw near to you. Because of your grace and the blood shed for us, we don't come to an angry or frustrated God, but to a God full of love who welcomes us in, forgives us, cleanses us and brings us into his presence. What an amazing thing.

Like David said, like a weaned child with its mother, so perfectly content can we be in your presence. Why do we resist so often? Help us come quickly and humbly to receive the peace, grace, rest, encouragement and joy of being in your presence. We pray that for everyone listening today. In Jesus' name, amen.
